title: Ally guide wire contract
description: The single source of truth for what crosses the wire between ally-be, the learner app (ally-web) and the guide voice worker (ally-ai-learn). Edit this file, then run `node scripts/guide-contract/codegen.mjs` from ally-be to regenerate the TypeScript and Python copies. Only the JSON Schema subset the generator understands may be used: object (properties / required / additionalProperties), string (enum / const / maxLength), integer, number, boolean, null, array (items), $ref to #/$defs, oneOf of objects discriminated by a `type` const, and the custom `x-extends` keyword (single inheritance between object $defs). Plan: plans/ally-guide/plan.md §9.

GuideMode.description: Safety mode of a thread (plan §6.2). REAL_CASE and PII are per-message overlays, not modes.

GuideChannel.description: How a message reached the thread.

GuideItemType.description: Mirror of the Track 2.0 item types (ally-be TrackItemType).

GuideCardPresentation.description: Where a card opens: in the conversation, in the right-hand Shelf, or full screen in the Theatre (plan §5.2). Fixed per item type.

GuideTone.description: Celebration intensity, capped by trigger warnings and mode (plan §4.7).

GuideFailureCode.description: Why a turn failed (plan §9.3). The client maps each to a designed state in Ally's voice.

GuideCard.description: One unit in the conversation (plan §5.6). `payload` is learner-safe by construction: it never carries answer keys (plan §6.4).

GuideMemorySource.description: One of the learner's own messages a memory note was drawn from: the answer to "why does Ally remember this?". A message the learner has since deleted is absent.

excerpt.description: The learner's words, at most 200 characters.

GuideMemoryView.description: GET /v1/guide/memory returns an array of these: what Ally remembers about the learner in this organisation (plan §8.1), each with its provenance.

GuideCrisisState.description: The fixed crisis response on screen (plan §6.3): sent as crisis.response, and in bootstrap while the thread is in CRISIS so a reload keeps the card.

GuideFinaleDoor.description: One of the finale's three doors (plan §4.3 endgame). field_assignment: try one thing on the next real shift and come back to tell Ally. spaced_recall: book a short look back — the client saves `suggestedAt` (or the learner's own pick) with PUT threads/:id/appointment and purpose spaced_recall. mentor: leave a line for the next learner (`available` is false until advice lines ship; hide it then).

suggestedAt.description: spaced_recall: seven days from the finale, ISO.

maxChars.description: mentor: the advice line's length limit.

GuideFinalePayload.description: `card.payload` of a `finale` card (plan §3 stage 13, §5.10), presented when the course completes. Every part is the learner's own or Ally's noticing, never a score; a part with nothing behind it is null or empty and the reveal skips it. `hushed` (heavy trigger warnings, or a hard moment) means a quiet reveal: no festive motion.

firstMove.description: The notebook's first move beside an invitation to answer the same question now. `question` is what Ally had asked, when it is known.

noticings.description: Ally's noticing moments in this course, oldest first.

GuideSceneView.description: A chapter scene as bootstrap returns it: what scene.opened and scene.closed said, with the seqs they were sent at.

closedSeq.description: Null while the scene is open.

receipt.description: Present once the scene has closed.

GuideAnchor.description: Context attached to a turn by 'Ask about this' (plan §5.8).

GuideEventBase.description: Every SSE event: `event: <type>`, `id: <seq>`, `data: <this JSON>`. `seq` is monotonic per thread; ephemeral events reuse the last durable seq and set `durable: false`.

GuideEvent.description: Every event the thread stream can carry, discriminated by `type`.

intent.description: A structured nudge from the UI instead of free text: start, the Continue chip, a locked-item peek, the Not now chip (which starts Ally's steering cooldown), or "I'm safe right now" on the crisis card (CRISIS → CARE, plan §6.3 step 5).

GuideCardEventRequest.description: POST /v1/guide/threads/:id/cards/:cardId/events. Claims are verified against progress on the server.

GuideVoiceTurnRequest.description: Voice worker → ally-be, POST /v1/guide/voice/turns. Authenticated with the service API key plus `token` (the voice-session token bound to thread, user and tenant).

GuideVoiceFrameStart.description: First line of every voice turn stream: the turn's id, so a barge-in mid-stream can still name the turn it cut off.

kind.description: "crisis" on the fixed crisis message (plan §6.3 step 4): the worker speaks it slowly and keeps the session open. Absent on ordinary replies.

GuideVoiceFrameCardHint.description: A short speakable line when a card appears on screen ('I've put the article on your right').

GuideVoiceFrame.description: One NDJSON line of the voice turn response stream.

GuideAvailability.description: Whether the guided experience is available for a course, for this caller (plan §9.1).

languages.description: Language codes the course is published in.

reason.description: Why guided is false; null when it is available.

GuideAccess.description: The same access answer classic gives (`GET /v1/learn/tracks/:id/access`).

reason.description: A TrackAccessDenialReason when access is refused.

GuideSpineItem.description: One item on the Spine (plan §5.2). State mirrors classic progression exactly.

hasWarnings.description: The item carries content warnings; the UI may hush around it.

GuideSpine.description: The whole course as the Spine draws it.

GuideMessageView.description: A transcript message as the learner sees it (no model internals).

GuidePrefs.description: The learner's own settings for Ally (plan §8.1 guide_learner_prefs).

GuideAllowance.description: An anonymous visitor's messages left today on this course (plan Appendix A). The client shows a quiet counter once two or fewer remain, and the sign-in card at zero.

GuideVisitorCreated.description: POST /v1/guide/public/visitors — the visitor token. Only its hash is stored; the browser keeps it and sends it as the x-guide-visitor header, and once more when signing in so the conversation is claimed.

GuideThreadOpened.description: POST tracks/:trackId/threads (signed in or visitor). `claim` says what happened to a visitor conversation sent along with x-guide-visitor: it became this thread (claimed), was folded into the learner's existing one (merged), or there was none (none).

GuideMicroActivity.description: A side quest's content on its card (`card.payload.activity`, plan §4.6). Learner-safe: options carry no key and no feedback until answered.

GuideMicroActivityRequest.description: POST threads/:id/micro-activities/:cardId/responses: `answers` for questions with options, `text` for a written answer.

GuideMicroActivityResult.description: The answer, marked (questions) or noted (written). Ungraded: it never affects progress or XP.

GuideAdviceLineRequest.description: POST /v1/guide/tracks/:trackId/advice: the mentor door. A finisher of the course leaves one line for those who come after; it can be rewritten until it is reviewed.

GuideAdviceLineView.description: The learner's own advice line, and where it is in review.

GuideAdviceLines.description: GET /v1/guide/tracks/:trackId/advice: approved, anonymous advice from finishers in the learner's organisation (empty until enough have finished; render each line as a quotation, as plain text), and the learner's own line (absent when they have not written one).

lastEventSeq.description: Resume the event stream after this seq.

seq.description: Event seq it was presented at, for ordering in the feed.

GuideBootstrap.description: GET /v1/guide/tracks/:trackId/bootstrap — everything the journey needs to draw itself. Absent keys mean not applicable (no thread yet, no access).

scenes.description: Every chapter scene of the thread, oldest first (plan §5.5), so a reload can group the feed: an entry belongs to a scene when its seq is at or after `openedSeq` and before `closedSeq` (or the scene is still open). The scenes' own title cards are not repeated in `cards`.
